name: wait
description: What a program's loop waits on, for every component that works while it runs: a Set of any number of descriptors (sockets on Windows), each with its Interest and a key, and deadlines on the monotonic clock, level-triggered on epoll (Linux), kqueue (macOS), socket notifications (Windows 11, Server 2022) or WSAPoll (earlier Windows), what is ready reported as Ready, the same on every system, and every refusal as a SetError; tokens of one Set refused by another; Owned entries that only close takes out, closing the descriptor once; a Waker for other threads; a component's Wait (up to two descriptors and a timeout), which a Set follows or block waits on alone; and a pool of at most 32 threads with a cancellable FIFO line (unsafe spawn, a Ticket that cancels when dropped), and the close-on-exec pipe (Linux and macOS) or non-inherited loopback socket pair (Windows) that says the work is done.
